issue.title: Map how amp_flint_par's output depends on --procs

labels.name: win2
labels.description: Task for win2, the Windows desktop

issue.body:
**What.** Map how `amp_flint_par.py`'s output depends on `--procs`: run one small case (for example ω/ω∞ = 1.10, K 25, J 1000, 960 bits, `--fit phys --mf 6:12`) with `--procs` 1, 2, 3 and 4, twice each, on one machine. Name the first differing string between every pair. If it is cheap, test the candidate mechanism from #229: `_products` sums the workers' partial results per group, so the order of summation follows the worker count. Recommended by win2 in #229's summary.

**Why.** #229 found that --procs 2 on win2 equals macm3's T153 file bit for bit, while --procs 3 differs from it first at f 33_3 and at σ₁₆ by 1.5e-19. #82 used 3 workers, T155-win2 4, T153-macm3 2 and #202 3, so which files can be compared bit for bit depends on this.

**Acceptance (can fail).**
- Equal counts give equal bits. A failure of this is the main finding.
- Each pair of counts is equal or not, with the first differing string named.
- If the mechanism is tested, a summation in a fixed order makes all counts equal, or it doesn't.

**Depends on.** #229.

comments.body: Coordinator: assigned to win2, beside #213. From `solver/inner_amp/`, Normal priority, raw folder `I236-win2/`, for N in 1, 2, 3, 4 and runs r1, r2, in batches that fit beside #213: `python -u amp_flint_par.py 1.10 25 1000 960 --procs N --fit phys --mf 6:12 --out <raw>\I236-win2\sigF_w1.10_K25_J1000_procsN_rR.json`. Compare every pair (strings, sigma_err, f, fit_info), naming the first differing key. #228 still starts when #213 ends.

**Started, win2, 2026-11-09 07:05:35 UTC.** Checkout `D:\choptuik-large-d` (main at 188853c), Python 3.14.10 (`venv-t177`, python-flint 0.9.0 / FLINT 3.6.0), BIOS 3.40, Normal priority, no affinity. Command, from `solver/inner_amp/`: `amp_flint_par.py 1.10 25 1000 960 --procs N --fit phys --mf 6:12 --out I236-win2/sigF_w1.10_K25_J1000_procsN_rR.json` for N = 1, 2, 3, 4 and R = r1, r2. Two batches of four runs (the four counts of r1 at once, then r2), so 4 mains plus 10 workers at most beside #213's 12 processes, expected about 1 to 1.5 h per batch under that load (K 25 took 3218 s at 3 processes in #202), about 2 to 3 GB per run. `compare_236.py` will compare every pair and name the first differing key. The optional mechanism test (a fixed summation order in `_products`) comes after the map, from a copy of the module in the raw folder, with no change to main. #228 still starts when #213 ends. Raw folder `I236-win2/`.

**Progress, 2026-11-09 09:13 UTC. Batch r1 is done, batch r2 started at 09:09:45.** All four runs of r1 (K 25, J 1000, ω/ω∞ = 1.10, 960 bits, `--fit phys --mf 6:12`, `--procs` 1, 2, 3, 4) ended with exit 0:

| `--procs` | wall (r1) | process tree (seen at 07:12 to 09:04) |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | 2719 s | 2.7 GB |
| 3 | 3292 s | 3.2 GB |
| 2 | 4369 s | 3.8 GB |
| 1 | 7450 s | 1.8 GB |

Beside #213 (three nodes, 12 processes) the machine ran at 28 to 123% utilization (Windows processor-utility counter), package power 54 to 194 W, free memory 29.0 to 49.1 GB of 95.5 GB between 07:09 and 09:09, and no crash, WHEA or Kernel-Power event (#204's hourly posts have the table).

**First comparison, r1 only** (`compare_236.py` logic, timing keys and `procs` dropped). Every one of the 6 pairs of counts differs, and in the same way:

| section | result for every pair of counts |
|---|---|
| `sigma_str` (13 strings, 20 digits) | equal |
| `sigma_err` | equal |
| `f` (all 78 entries) | equal |
| `sigma`, `sigma_rad`, `K`, `J`, `prec`, `mf`, `fit` ... | equal |
| `fit_info` (Mf, err, resid) | Mf equal in all 91 families; err and resid differ in 11 families, the first at `21_19`; the others are 21_21, 23_15, 23_17, 23_19, 23_21, 23_23, 25_19, 25_21, 25_23, 25_25 |

In each of those 11 families the four counts give four different (err, resid) pairs, so no two counts are equal; the largest relative difference between two runs is 1.29 in err and 0.095 in resid. So at K 25 the process count changes only the fit's own error and residual estimates in 11 families from order 21 on, and none of σ, `sigma_err` or `f`. (At K 33, #229, it reached σ₁₆ at 1.5e-19.)

**Not yet answered:** whether equal counts give equal bits. Batch r2 (the same four runs) ends by about 10:25 for 4, 3 and 2 and about 11:15 for `--procs 1`; then `compare_236.py` runs on all eight files. After r2 the fixed-summation variant batch (`amp_flint_par_fixsum.py`, one run per count) starts by itself. Progress posts continue hourly here.

**Progress, 2026-11-09 10:05 UTC.** Batch r2 (started 09:09:45) is running: `--procs 4` is done (exit 0, 2672 s, r1 took 2719 s), `--procs 3` is at order 23 after 2485 s, `--procs 2` at order 21 after 2385 s, `--procs 1` at order 19 after 2856 s (r1: 7450 s in all, so the last ends near 11:15 UTC). Process trees: 1.0 GB (1 proc), 3.4 GB (2), 5.4 GB (3). The machine, beside #213, ran at 61 to 117% utilization with free memory 24.9 to 37.6 GB between 09:14 and 09:54 (#204's hourly post has the sensor table), and no crash or WHEA event.

**First pair of equal counts: `--procs 4` r1 against r2 is bit for bit equal** (`sigma_str`, `sigma_err`, `f`, `fit_info` and every other key, timing keys and `procs` dropped), so for 4 workers the two runs reproduce each other although the four counts differ among themselves in 11 families of `fit_info` (r1 post). The other three counts follow when their r2 runs end (3 near 10:10, 2 near 10:25, 1 near 11:15). Then `compare_236.py` runs on all eight files and the fixed-summation variant batch starts by itself.

**Progress, 2026-11-09 11:00 UTC.** Batch r2 (started 09:09:45): `--procs 4` (2672 s), 3 (3235 s) and 2 (4319 s) ended with exit 0, the `--procs 1` run is at order 23 after 5538 s and should end near 11:15 (r1: 7450 s). Process tree of the running one 2.0 GB. The machine, beside #213, ran at 55 to 85% utilization, 90 to 150 W and 31.1 to 44.0 GB free memory from 09:59 to 10:54 (#204's post has the table), with no crash or WHEA event.

**Equal counts give equal bits, for 4, 3 and 2:** `--procs` 2 r1 against r2, 3 r1 against r2 and 4 r1 against r2 are each bit for bit equal (`sigma_str`, `sigma_err`, `f`, `fit_info`, every other key, timing keys and `procs` dropped). The fourth pair, `--procs 1`, follows at 11:15. Together with r1's finding that the four counts differ among themselves in 11 families of `fit_info` (and nowhere else at K 25), the count changes the fit's err and resid estimates deterministically: the same count reproduces itself, a different count does not. After the last r2 run, `compare_236.py` runs on all eight files and the fixed-summation batch starts by itself.

**Progress, 2026-11-09 11:58 UTC.** **The eight base runs are done and compared** (`compare_236.py`, exit 0, selftest ok; `compare_236.log` in `I236-win2/`):

| `--procs` | r1 wall | r2 wall | r1 against r2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 7450 s | 7387 s | **bit for bit equal** |
| 2 | 4369 s | 4319 s | **bit for bit equal** |
| 3 | 3292 s | 3235 s | **bit for bit equal** |
| 4 | 2719 s | 2672 s | **bit for bit equal** |

So equal counts give equal bits, 4 of 4 pairs. The six pairs of different counts all differ, the same way each time (24 run pairs): `sigma_str`, `sigma_err`, `f` and every other key are equal, and `fit_info` differs in err and resid in 11 of 91 families (21_19, 21_21, 23_15 to 23_23, 25_19 to 25_25), Mf equal, the first at `21_19`. Each count is its own class of two runs, so no two counts reproduce each other at K 25, J 1000.

**Mechanism test, running** (`amp_flint_par_fixsum.py`: the module of main with `_products` summing each order's products in task order, whatever the count; K 13 smoke test: the variant at counts 1, 2, 3 equals the original at count 1): the four runs started 11:13:13 and are at order 17 (`--procs 1`, 1898 s), 19 (2, 1850 s) and 21 (3 and 4, 2141 and 1856 s). They end near 12:20 to 12:40 for counts 4 to 2 and about 13:15 for count 1. The result is whether the four variant runs are equal to each other, and whether they equal the original `--procs 1` run, the serial association they imitate. Machine: beside #213, 56 to 118% utilization, 96 to 184 W, 32.5 to 39.9 GB free memory over the last hour (#204's post has the table), no crash or WHEA event.

**Progress, 2026-11-09 12:55 UTC. The mechanism is confirmed so far.** The fixed-summation runs (`amp_flint_par_fixsum.py`, `_products` adds each order's products per group in task order, whatever the worker count; K 25, J 1000, 1.10) with `--procs` 4, 3 and 2 are done (exit 0; 3407, 3939 and 4894 s), the `--procs 1` one is at order 23 after 5614 s and ends near 13:15 UTC. `compare_236.py`'s pair test on the three finished ones, timing keys and `procs` dropped:

| pair | result |
|---|---|
| fixed-summation `--procs` 2 against 3, 2 against 4, 3 against 4 | **bit for bit equal** (all three) |
| fixed-summation `--procs` 2, 3 and 4 against the original `--procs 1` run (r1) | **bit for bit equal** (all three) |
| fixed-summation `--procs` 2, 3, 4 against the original run with the same count (r1) | differ, `fit_info` err/resid in 11 of 91 families, first at `21_19` (the base-run difference) |

So with one summation order every count gives the same bits, and they are the bits of the original serial path (`--procs 1`, which sums the tasks of an order in order), while the original with 2, 3 or 4 workers differs from it. The dependence of `amp_flint_par.py`'s output on `--procs` at K 25 comes from the order of summation of the workers' partial products, as hypothesised in #229. The fixed-summation `--procs 1` run, which completes the 4-of-4 check, follows at about 13:15 UTC; then the closing summary.

Machine, beside #213: 68 to 117% utilization, 103.5 to 162 W, free memory 16.9 to 33.7 GB over 11:54 to 12:44 (16.9 GB at 11:54:35 is the lowest of the day, see #204's post), no crash or WHEA event.

**Results, win2, 2026-11-09 13:25 UTC.** Twelve runs of `amp_flint_par.py 1.10 25 1000 960 --fit phys --mf 6:12` on Python 3.14.10, python-flint 0.9.0 / FLINT 3.6.0, Normal priority, no affinity, beside #213: `--procs` 1, 2, 3 and 4 twice each (r1 and r2), and once each with a fixed-summation variant. All exit 0. Walls (r1 / r2 / fixed): 1 process 7450 / 7387 / 7459 s, 2: 4369 / 4319 / 4894 s, 3: 3292 / 3235 / 3939 s, 4: 2719 / 2672 / 3407 s (not a clean timing, the load beside them changed). Process trees 0.7 to 6.6 GB; the machine ran at 28 to 123% utilization and 54 to 194 W, free memory 16.9 to 49 GB, with no crash or WHEA event (#204's hourly posts).

**Acceptance 1: equal counts give equal bits. Met.** `compare_236.py` (exit 0), timing keys and `procs` dropped:

| `--procs` | r1 against r2 |
|---|---|
| 1 | bit for bit equal |
| 2 | bit for bit equal |
| 3 | bit for bit equal |
| 4 | bit for bit equal |

**Acceptance 2: each pair of counts, with the first differing string named.** All six pairs of different counts differ (24 run pairs), the same way every time:

| section | result |
|---|---|
| `sigma_str` (13 strings, 20 digits), `sigma_err`, `f` (78 entries), `sigma`, `sigma_rad`, all other keys | equal |
| `fit_info`, Mf | equal in all 91 families |
| `fit_info`, err and resid | differ in 11 of 91 families; **first differing key `21_19`**, then 21_21, 23_15, 23_17, 23_19, 23_21, 23_23, 25_19, 25_21, 25_23, 25_25 |

In each of the 11 families the four counts give four different values, so no two counts reproduce each other at K 25. The largest relative difference between two runs is 1.29 in err and 0.095 in resid. At K 25 the count changes only the fit's own error and residual estimates, from order 21 on; at K 33 (#229) it also reached σ₁₆ at 1.5e-19.

**Acceptance 3: a summation in a fixed order makes all counts equal. Met.** `amp_flint_par_fixsum.py` imports the module of `solver/inner_amp` (main, unchanged) and replaces `AmpPar._products`: every task of an order is a chunk of its own, dealt to the workers as before, and the main adds the single products per group in task order, the association of the serial path. Results (`compare_fixsum.log`):

| comparison | result |
|---|---|
| fixed summation with 1, 2, 3 and 4 processes, all six pairs | **bit for bit equal** |
| each of them against the original `--procs 1` run (r1 and r2) | **bit for bit equal** |
| fixed summation with 2, 3 or 4 against the original run with the same count (r1 and r2) | differ, in the same 11 `fit_info` families |

So the summation order of the workers' partial products is the source of the dependence, as hypothesised in #229. A K 13 smoke test (`smoke/`) of the variant at 1, 2 and 3 processes against the original at 1 ran first and was equal.

**Controls:** `compare_236.py --selftest` plants a changed digit in one sigma string, one `f` entry, one `fit_info` entry and one `sigma_err` entry and finds each at its key, and a differing pair of equal counts must give exit 1 (ok). The variant is not a trivial pass: it agrees with the original only at `--procs 1`, and differs from the originals at 2, 3 and 4 exactly where the base runs differ.

**Limits.** One case, K 25, J 1000, 1.10 on one machine. The cause is shown for the products' summation at K 25; whether the whole of #229's K 33 difference at σ₁₆ comes from it was not run. The variant's wall times are above the originals for 2, 3 and 4 workers (+12%, +20%, +25%), but the load beside them differed between the batches, so the cost of the per-task messages is not measured.

**Discrepancies:** none beyond #229's (output depends on `--procs`), which this explains.

**Raw:** `I236-win2/` at commit d4562f7 of choptuik-large-d-raw (twelve JSONs and logs, `exits.txt`, `exits_fixsum.txt`, `compare_236.py` with logs, `compare_fixsum.log`, `amp_flint_par_fixsum.py`, `run_i236.sh`, `run_i236_fixsum.sh`, README with the results).

**Recommended tasks**

1. **Make `amp_flint_par.py`'s output independent of `--procs`.** What: in a worktree, replace `_products`' per-worker partial sums by the fixed-order summation of `amp_flint_par_fixsum.py` (or an equivalent fixed-order reduction), measure the wall cost of the per-task messages with a clean run (K 25 at 1, 2, 3 and 4 processes alone), and rerun #229's K 33 case with 2 and 3 processes. Why: it removes the need for the same count in every bit-for-bit comparison (#202, #228, any cross-machine check) and gives the serial path's bits at any speed. Acceptance: counts 1 to 4 equal bit for bit at K 25, K 33 at 2 and 3 workers equal bit for bit (and, if the serial K 33 path is run, equal to it), and the wall cost reported; it can fail. Open question for the coordinator and Nathan: files already made with the old code (all of #82, T153, T155) stay as they are, they are valid to the 1e-19 scale seen. Depends on #236.
2. **Does the K 33 difference at σ₁₆ come only from the summation order?** What: K 33, J 1000 at 1.10 with `amp_flint_par_fixsum.py` at 2 and 3 processes (about 3 h each, together beside #213 or after it) and compare with #202's and #229's files. Why: #229 and #236 together suggest it, but K 33 was not run with the variant. Acceptance: the two variant runs are equal to each other, and either equal to the serial-order K 33 value or not, so the result separates the summation order from other sources at K 33. Depends on #236; it is also satisfied by task 1's K 33 check.

#236 is closed with this comment: the twelve runs are complete and the three acceptance conditions are answered. The optional mechanism test was run.

Closed by win2: the twelve runs are complete and the three acceptance conditions are answered above (equal counts give equal bits, the six pairs of counts differ first at fit_info 21_19, and a fixed summation order makes all counts equal and equal to the serial path).
